newsitem.title: UK: SHELL SEES RISING OIL SUPPLY, LOW REFINERY OUTAGES.
newsitem.headline: SHELL SEES RISING OIL SUPPLY, LOW REFINERY OUTAGES.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell said on Thursday it expected rising world crude oil output later this year and plentiful product supplies.

"The industry outlook is for continued increases in crude supply from the North Sea and ample product supply due to low refinery maintenance in the third quarter," the company said on announcing results for the second quarter.
Shell said complex refining margins for the second quarter of the year improved year-on-year to $2.10 a barrel versus $1.95 last year.
"Refining saw a strong improvement, with the benefit of higher industry margins in Europe enhanced by higher utilisation and lower operating costs," it said.
Margins were supported by strength in the U.S. gasoline market, it added.
Singapore margins for the second quarter were $2.40 versus $3 a barrel for the same period last year.
"Margins have been adversely affected by the increased supply from new refinery capacity," Shell said.
Marketing performance improved in all regions and there was "a relative improvement in the UK retail market," in the second quarter.
The company said it expected the chemicals sector to improve in the remainder of the year as a result of strong cracker economics.
